<h2 class="section-title">India National Politics</h2>

<ul class="digest-points">
  <li><strong>Parliamentary deadlock:</strong> Opposition parties continue to protest in Parliament despite appeals from Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and government offers to have Home Minister Amit Shah deliver a statement.<span class="source-chips"><a href="https://news.google.?oc=5&amp;hl=en-US&amp;gl=US&amp;ceid=US%3Aen" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">I5</a> <a href="https://news.google.?oc=5&amp;hl=en-US&amp;gl=US&amp;ceid=US%3Aen" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">I6</a></span></li>
  <li><strong>Legislative progress:</strong> The Lok Sabha has passed the Tribunals Reforms Bill to enhance efficiency, while the government faces opposition demands for a total rollback of the FCRA Bill despite hints at a Joint Parliamentary Committee review.<span class="source-chips"><a href="https://news.google.?oc=5&amp;hl=en-US&amp;gl=US&amp;ceid=US%3Aen" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">I4</a> <a href="https://news.google.?oc=5&amp;hl=en-US&amp;gl=US&amp;ceid=US%3Aen" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">I9</a></span></li>
</ul>

<h2 class="section-title">Policy and Institutions</h2>

<ul class="digest-points">
  <li><strong>Financial and banking legislation:</strong> Parliament passed the Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill and a measure authorizing the government to permit bank charges on UPI transactions, though Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman clarified that no tax will be imposed on UPI itself.</li>
  <li><strong>Judicial and regulatory oversight:</strong> The government defended the Clinical Establishments Rules before the Supreme Court to ensure healthcare quality, while the Court noted that the acquittal of Ram Rahim in a journalist murder case warrants further consideration.</li>
</ul>
